result.title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
result.summary: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bias-variance tradeoff in terms of gradient direction, measuring how closely each method's gradient estimates align with the true policy gradient as batch size grows. Under a shared actor objective, we compare GRPO with PPO in control tasks, short-horizon math, and long-horizon terminal agents. Across more than 1,200 training runs, including 96 with LLMs, we find that PPO generally leads at small batch sizes, while GRPO often overtakes heavily bootstrapped PPO and reaches parity with lightly bootstrapped PPO at larger batches. At longer horizons and in more complex domains, GRPO needs larger batches to catch up to PPO's performance. Accounting for training compute, critics pay off at small budgets, but their returns diminish at larger budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在共享 actor 目标下比较带 critic 的 PPO 与无 critic 的 GRPO 的梯度方向偏差-方差权衡，用 batch size、critic 依赖程度和任务复杂度解释两者优劣，并在控制任务、短程数学与长程终端智能体上做了逾 1200 次训练（含 96 次 LLM），同时给出按训练计算量折算的结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于长程、复杂任务中 credit assignment 与 batch／计算预算如何交互的实证结论，可供核查 LVR 多步推理轨迹训练是否值得引入 critic 做细粒度贡献分配；但内容限于纯文本 RL 训练层面，不涉及视觉证据或 latent 状态生成，联系较弱。
